function_analysis: Stored functions F1-F5 apply (reject solar, emit to the sky window, decouple the envelope from the hot skin, keep it for 20 years against soiling/UV/cycling, passively). This round asks for concepts judged on temperature (surface or wall temperature, which drives the heat flux and the peak cooling load) and for a plant-derived sub-micron scattering surface that fixes the soiling weakness of open-porous white coats.

requirements.name: indoor_heat_gain_reduction
requirements.criterion: Clearly lowers the summer-day heat flux into the interior (roughly >20 %) versus the aged conventional white cool coating on the same envelope.

requirements.name: fully_passive
requirements.criterion: Works without electricity, pumps, fans or water supply; only sun, sky, wind and rain act on it.

requirements.name: weather_durability_20yr
requirements.criterion: Keeps its optical and thermal function (and adhesion) for at least 20 years under hot-climate UV, thermal cycling, rain, dust/sand and soiling without major maintenance.

requirements.name: bionic_mechanism
requirements.criterion: The working mechanism is actually derived from a biological model (plant, animal, microbe), not only labelled so.

requirements.name: building_practicality
requirements.criterion: Applicable as coating or facade structure on real buildings at acceptable cost, weight and glare, without toxic release.

analogues_considered: Cactus spines and pubescence (Ferocactus, Cephalocereus senilis; Nobel 1978): shade the apex and hold a still boundary layer, lowering apex maximum temperature by several K
Chinese tussah silkmoth (Antheraea pernyi) cocoon fibres: sub-micron air voids along the fibre give strong solar reflection and high mid-IR emissivity (Shi, Yu et al. 2018)
Birch bark phellem: betulin crystals inside closed, dead, air-filled cells make the bark white
Chalk dudleya (Dudleya brittonii) epicuticular wax: very high UV/visible reflectance
White flower petals: air-filled mesophyll scattering
objective_statement: Summer-day (24 h) heat flux into the conditioned interior through the sun-exposed roof and facades of a building in a hot climate, averaged over a 20-year service life, including UV ageing, weathering and soiling of the outer surface (not the value of a freshly applied clean surface).
baseline_statement: Conventional white acrylic/elastomeric cool-roof or facade coating (initial solar reflectance ~0.85, thermal emittance ~0.90) in its in-service aged and soiled condition (3-year aged solar reflectance ~0.65-0.70, as in CRRC ageing data), repainted every ~10 years, on the same insulated wall or roof.

candidates.title: Cactus-spine pile facade shade
candidates.summary: A 40 mm deep pile of white, UV-stable glass-ceramic rods (2 mm diameter) standing off the facade like the dense spine cover of barrel and old-man cacti, which shades the apex and holds a slow boundary layer, lowering its peak temperature. The pile intercepts ~90 % of direct sun in a volume that wind flushes with ambient air, so the absorbed heat is dumped to the air before it reaches the wall.

back_of_envelope.quantity: Reduction of daily-mean west-facade heat flux vs aged white paint on the wall (peak-hour wall temperature in brackets)
back_of_envelope.formula: Pile extinction kappa*L = 2.4 -> 9 % of sun reaches the wall; rods reflect 80 %. Peak (I=700, T_a=43 C): baseline wall excess (0.33*700 - 36)/15 = 13 K; design wall excess ~3 K -> peak flux (T_w - T_in) 31 K -> 21 K, -32 %. Daily mean (I=180, R_net=40): baseline excess 1.6 K vs design ~0.4 K (the pile also blocks the wall's sky view) -> q 11.6 -> 10.4 K*U, -10 %

candidates.main_risk: Against an already white wall the daily-mean gain is small (~10 %), because the pile also blocks the wall's radiative loss to the sky; dust, leaves and birds collect in the pile.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest known: perforated metal or ceramic brise-soleil and ventilated rainscreens; new is a deep, isotropic, wind-flushed spine pile that shades all sun angles without orientation-specific design, taken from cactus spine cover.
candidates.baseline: Conventional white acrylic facade coating, aged and soiled (SR 0.67, emittance 0.90), directly on the same insulated wall (U = 0.5 W/m2K).
candidates.inspiration_source: Cactus spine cover (Ferocactus acanthodes, Cephalocereus senilis): dense spines and hairs shade the stem apex and slow air near it; measured apex maximum temperatures drop by several K (Nobel 1978).
candidates.domain: Heat transfer in porous media / building physics
candidates.physical_mechanism: The pile is a porous layer that absorbs the solar fraction not reflected by the rods with an exponential (Beer-Lambert) profile and exchanges heat with wind-driven ambient air through a volumetric coefficient. Steady 1D energy balance in the pile: k_eff*T'' - H_v*(T - T_a) + S(x) = 0 with S = (1 - rho_rod)*kappa*I*exp(-kappa*(L - z)); the wall side couples to the wall conductance and receives the transmitted sun.

parameters.name: pile_depth
parameters.justification: Spine cover depth of barrel cacti is 2-5 cm.

parameters.name: extinction_coefficient
parameters.justification: kappa = n*d projected rod area per volume; 2 mm rods at ~8 mm spacing give ~60 1/m (kappa*L = 2.4).

parameters.name: rod_solar_reflectance
parameters.justification: White glass-ceramic rods, rain-washed and smooth.

parameters.name: pile_effective_conductivity
parameters.justification: Still-air plus radiative plus wind-dispersive conductivity of an open pile.

parameters.name: volumetric_air_exchange_coefficient
parameters.justification: h_rod*specific surface: h ~20 W/m2K on 2 mm rods times ~25 m2/m3 surface density.

parameters.name: wall_u_value
parameters.justification: Same wall as baseline.

parameters.name: solar_irradiance_daily_mean
parameters.justification: West facade, hot summer day.

candidates.title: Tussah-silk nanovoid glass-fibre shade screen
candidates.summary: A tensioned facade screen woven from glass fibres drawn with sub-micron longitudinal air voids, copying the fibres of the Chinese tussah silkmoth cocoon whose nanovoids scatter sunlight strongly and whose silk emits well in the mid-IR. The voided fibres make a thin fabric reflect ~83 % of sunlight while absorbing only ~7 %, so the ventilated screen stays near ambient temperature and the wall behind it sees mostly a cool screen instead of the sun.

back_of_envelope.quantity: Reduction of daily-mean west-facade heat flux vs aged white paint on the wall (peak wall temperature in brackets)
back_of_envelope.formula: Screen alpha 0.07, tau 0.10, eps 0.9, ventilated both sides h_c 10: peak screen excess (49 - 20)/20 = 1.5 K; wall receives 0.1*700*0.33 = 23 W/m2 + longwave from screen -> wall excess ~3 K vs 13 K for the bare painted wall; peak flux -32 %. Daily mean: wall excess ~0.4 K vs 1.6 K -> q -10 %.

candidates.main_risk: Drawing glass fibres with stable sub-micron voids at scale is unproven, and an ordinary PTFE-coated glass fabric screen already gives most of the benefit, so the bionic fibre adds only a few percent.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest known: PTFE-coated glass-fibre facade membranes and solar screens; new is the intrinsically white voided fibre (no coating that soils or yellows), from the tussah silk nanovoid structure.
candidates.baseline: Conventional white acrylic facade coating, aged and soiled (SR 0.67, emittance 0.90), directly on the same insulated wall.
candidates.inspiration_source: Antheraea pernyi (Chinese tussah silkmoth) cocoon fibres: randomly distributed sub-micron air voids along the fibre give high solar reflectance by transverse Anderson localisation and high mid-IR emissivity, keeping the pupa cool.
candidates.physical_mechanism: Sub-micron voids along glass fibres scatter visible and NIR light strongly, so a thin fabric reflects most sunlight and transmits ~10 %; the glass emits in 8-13 um. The screen, ventilated on both sides, stays within a few K of ambient; the wall behind it receives only the transmitted fraction plus longwave from a near-ambient screen. Modelled as steady 1D conduction through the wall with a Robin boundary at the wall surface that contains the transmitted solar, convection to cavity air and linearised longwave exchange with the screen at its own balance temperature.

parameters.name: screen_solar_absorptance
parameters.justification: Voided glass fabric; conventional PTFE-glass membranes absorb 0.10-0.20.

parameters.name: screen_solar_transmittance
parameters.justification: Dense weave with high scattering.

parameters.name: void_diameter
parameters.justification: Tussah silk voids are ~100-1000 nm; Mie optimum for sunlight near 200-400 nm.

parameters.name: screen_thermal_emittance
parameters.justification: Silicate glass emits strongly in 8-13 um.

parameters.name: cavity_convection_coefficient
parameters.justification: Ventilated cavity between screen and wall.

parameters.name: wall_u_value
parameters.justification: Same wall as baseline.

parameters.name: solar_irradiance_daily_mean
parameters.justification: West facade, hot summer day.

candidates.title: Birch-phellem closed-cell white coat
candidates.summary: A white mineral coat whose surface consists of closed, air-filled glass micro-cells (20-50 um) with sub-micron BaSO4 crystals embedded in the cell walls, copying birch bark, whose whiteness comes from betulin crystals inside closed dead phellem cells. The closed cells scatter like the open-porous beetle coat but give a smooth, sealed surface that dust cannot penetrate and rain can wash, fixing the main risk of open porous white coats.

back_of_envelope.quantity: Reduction of daily-mean roof heat flux vs aged white acrylic cool coating
back_of_envelope.formula: Clean SR 0.93, life-mean soiling loss 0.05 (sealed, smooth, rain-washed like glazes) -> SR 0.88, eps 0.93; q = 0.5*(0.12*300 + 150 - 0.93*85)/15.5 = 3.45 W/m2 vs baseline 0.5*(0.33*300 + 150 - 76.5)/15.5 = 5.56 W/m2 -> -38 %

candidates.main_risk: Closed cells break at the surface under sand abrasion and thermal cycling, reopening a porous, dirt-trapping surface; closing cells also lowers the scattering contrast, so clean SR may stay below 0.93.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest known: open-porous radiative cooling paints and hollow-glass-microsphere roof coatings; new is the combination of closed cells for dirt exclusion with sub-micron crystals in the cell walls for scattering, as in birch phellem.
candidates.baseline: Conventional white acrylic cool coating, aged and soiled (SR 0.67, emittance 0.90), on the same roof.
candidates.inspiration_source: Birch (Betula pendula) bark: dead phellem cells filled with air and with betulin crystals (~sub-micron) in and on the cell walls make a white, water-repellent, sealed outer bark.
candidates.physical_mechanism: Sub-micron BaSO4 crystals in the thin walls of closed glass cells scatter sunlight (index contrast 1.64/1.5 against air in the cells gives strong multiple scattering); the closed smooth surface limits dust penetration so soiling stays superficial and washable; silicate glass and sulfate emit in 8-13 um. Same steady 1D roof conduction with sol-air boundary as the reference concepts.

parameters.name: solar_reflectance
parameters.justification: Scattering in closed-cell walls with sub-micron crystals; slightly lower than an open network.

parameters.name: aged_reflectance_loss
parameters.justification: Sealed smooth surface soils like glazed ceramics, which lose 0.03-0.08.

parameters.name: thermal_emittance
parameters.justification: Silicate glass and sulfate bands.

parameters.name: cell_size
parameters.justification: Birch phellem cells are 20-40 um.

parameters.name: crystal_size
parameters.justification: Mie optimum for solar scattering.

parameters.name: roof_u_value
parameters.justification: Same roof as baseline.
